raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Motivation

Two lines block the host until the GPU has drained its queue, so the scheduler cannot prepare the next batch while the GPU works:

1. `AiterIndicesUpdaterPrefill` (normal extend) fills the tail of `kv_indices` from `kv_indptr[-1]`, a device scalar: slicing at it is a
   device-to-host read.
2. `ForwardBatch` speculative M-RoPE positions copy the per-request M-RoPE deltas (host tensors) with `torch.stack(...).to(device)`, a
   pageable, synchronizing copy, in every draft/verify cycle that has a multimodal request.

A torch profile (with stacks) of Qwen3.8-27B on MI355X, TP1, MTP 3/1/4, image requests (768x1024 + 1k text / 64 output tokens, 16
concurrent) showed the host blocked 844 ms over 4 prefill batches in (1), paid by the target extend and again by the EAGLE draft extend, and
162 ms over 20 draft/verify cycles in (2). With speculative decoding the image workload ran at 85% of the no-SD throughput, with the GPU
idle about half of the time.

## Modifications

1. The tail fill slices at `paged_kernel_lens_sum` (host int) instead of `kv_indptr[-1]`. Same offset: `kv_indptr[bs]` is the cumsum of
   `paged_kernel_lens`, whose sum is `paged_kernel_lens_sum`, which already sizes the buffer.
2. The M-RoPE deltas are copied with `async_h2d_stack` (pinned staging, non-blocking) instead of `torch.stack(...).to(device)`.

No numeric change by construction. The two commits are independent and can be split if preferred.

## Accuracy Tests

Setup: MI355X, `amd/Qwen3.8-27B-Quark-AWQ-MXFP4`, `--attention-backend aiter --kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3`, MTP 3/1/4
(`--speculative-algorithm EAGLE --speculative-num-steps 3 --speculative-eagle-topk 1 --speculative-num-draft-tokens 4`).

- Greedy outputs, upstream main 8080507c3e + #47430 with and without this PR (TP1, 50 ShareGPT prompts, 256 tokens, batch size 1):
  identical, 50/50. (#47430 is used as the base because without it the verify attention fallback makes greedy MTP output vary from
  run to run on this setup.)
- Upstream main 8080507c3e + this PR starts with MTP and serves text and image requests at TP1 (accept length 2.71) and TP2 (2.70).
- GSM8K (5-shot, all 1319 questions, `sglang.test.few_shot_gsm8k`) on the Qwen3.8 build below with this change (and #47430,
  #47431), MTP 3/1/4 + `--enable-linear-replayssm-spec`: 0.930, no invalid answers (no speculative decoding, without this change: 0.933).

## Speed Tests and Profiling

The two changed lines are the same on current main as on the build these numbers come from (a Qwen3.8 build of main: e732f5d41e +
14 open AMD Qwen3.8 PRs, among them #39912, #39998, #43785, #47154). MI355X TP1; SD = MTP 3/1/4 + `--enable-linear-replayssm-spec` with #47430 and #47431 applied;
output tok/s with `python -m sglang.bench_serving` (random / image datasets, range ratio 0.8), all four arms on the same GPU, one after another,
% of the no-SD baseline without this change:

| workload | no SD | no SD + this PR | SD | SD + this PR |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| image 768x1024 + 1k text / 64 out, 16 concurrent | 684.0 | 699.9 (102.3%) | 579.0 (84.6%) | 684.8 (100.1%) |
| image 768x1024 + 1k text / 64 out, 4 concurrent | 394.6 | 395.3 (100.2%) | 383.2 (97.1%) | 443.2 (112.3%) |
| image 768x1024 + 8k text / 64 out, 16 concurrent | 262.4 | 263.6 (100.5%) | 239.7 (91.4%) | 248.9 (94.9%) |
| text 8k / 1k out, 16 concurrent | 1582.1 | 1569.6 (99.2%) | 1780.5 (112.5%) | 1800.8 (113.8%) |
| text 60k / 600 out, 4 concurrent | 236.6 | 236.3 (99.9%) | 257.3 (108.7%) | 260.7 (110.2%) |

Image requests gain the most: with SD each image prefill batch paid the extend sync twice (target and draft) and every draft/verify cycle
paid the M-RoPE copy. Without SD only one extend per prefill batch blocked and the M-RoPE path is not used, so the change is neutral there.

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the Format code with pre-commit guide (pre-commit passes on the changed files).
- [ ] Add unit tests: none added (no behaviour change); the registered tests around these paths pass on MI355X (196 passed, 44 subtests passed: test_aiter_asm_prefill_gather, test_next_verify_prep, test_lora_spec_verify_batch_info, test_schedule_batch_out_of_place).
- [ ] Update documentation: not needed.
- [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results (above).
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style guidance.

files.patch:
@@ -4975,8 +4975,10 @@ def update_single_wrapper(
                 self.req_to_token.shape[1],
             )
 
-            token_num = kv_indptr[-1]
-            kv_indices[token_num:] = kv_indices[0]
+            # The slice start is kv_indptr[bs], already known on the host as
+            # paged_kernel_lens_sum; slicing at the device value would block
+            # the host until the GPU drains.
+            kv_indices[paged_kernel_lens_sum:] = kv_indices[0]
 
             extend_lens = seq_lens - prefix_lens

@@ -0,0 +1,88 @@
+"""kv_indices of the aiter prefill path are padded without a host read.
+
+AiterIndicesUpdaterPrefill pads kv_indices past the last real index with the
+first one. It must not read kv_indptr back for that: a host read stalls the CPU
+until the GPU drains, once per prefill, and leaves the GPU idle while the next
+step is prepared.
+"""
+
+import unittest
+from types import SimpleNamespace
+
+import torch
+
+from sglang.srt.layers.attention.aiter_backend import AiterIndicesUpdaterPrefill
+from sglang.test.ci.ci_register import register_amd_ci
+
+register_amd_ci(est_time=10, suite="stage-b-test-1-gpu-small-amd")
+
+
+@unittest.skipUnless(torch.cuda.is_available(), "Test requires a GPU")
+class TestAiterPrefillIndicesUpdater(unittest.TestCase):
+    def _update(self, seq_lens, prefix_lens, seq_lens_sum):
+        device = "cuda"
+        bs = len(seq_lens)
+        width = max(seq_lens) + 8
+        g = torch.Generator().manual_seed(bs)
+        # Row 0 is the padding row; requests use rows 1..bs of shuffled slots.
+        req_to_token = (
+            torch.randperm((bs + 1) * width, generator=g)
+            .to(torch.int32)
+            .reshape(bs + 1, width)
+            .to(device)
+        )
+        updater = SimpleNamespace(
+            kv_indptr=torch.zeros(bs + 2, dtype=torch.int32, device=device),
+            qo_indptr=torch.zeros(bs + 2, dtype=torch.int32, device=device),
+            req_to_token=req_to_token,
+            kv_index_translator=None,
+        )
+        args = (
+            torch.arange(1, bs + 1, dtype=torch.int64, device=device),
+            torch.tensor(seq_lens, dtype=torch.int64, device=device),
+            seq_lens_sum,
+            torch.tensor(prefix_lens, dtype=torch.int64, device=device),
+        )
+        # Compile the index kernel first, then check that no call syncs.
+        AiterIndicesUpdaterPrefill.update_single_wrapper(
+            updater, *args, None, None, plan=None
+        )
+        torch.cuda.synchronize()
+        torch.cuda.set_sync_debug_mode("error")
+        try:
+            AiterIndicesUpdaterPrefill.update_single_wrapper(
+                updater, *args, None, None, plan=None
+            )
+        finally:
+            torch.cuda.set_sync_debug_mode(0)
+        return updater, req_to_token.cpu()
+
+    def _check(self, seq_lens, prefix_lens, seq_lens_sum):
+        updater, req_to_token = self._update(seq_lens, prefix_lens, seq_lens_sum)
+        kv_indices = updater.kv_indices.cpu()
+        self.assertEqual(kv_indices.numel(), seq_lens_sum + 256)
+        expected = torch.cat([req_to_token[i + 1, :n] for i, n in enumerate(seq_lens)])
+        total = expected.numel()
+        self.assertTrue(torch.equal(kv_indices[:total], expected))
+        # Everything past the last real index repeats the first one.
+        self.assertTrue(
+            torch.equal(
+                kv_indices[total:], expected[:1].expand(len(kv_indices) - total)
+            )
+        )
+        extend = torch.tensor(seq_lens) - torch.tensor(prefix_lens)
+        self.assertEqual(
+            updater.qo_indptr[: len(seq_lens) + 1].tolist(),
+            [0, *extend.cumsum(0).tolist()],
+        )
+
+    def test_single_sequence(self):
+        self._check([16384], [0], 16384)
+        self._check([40000], [23616], 40000)
+
+    def test_several_sequences(self):
+        self._check([300, 1, 4096], [0, 0, 1000], 4397)
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    unittest.main()
